newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-LEHMAN BEMOANS POOR PUTTING AFTER 68.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEHMAN BEMOANS POOR PUTTING AFTER 68.

text.p: British Open champion Tom Lehman complained about his putting despite finishing one stroke off the lead after the first round of the South Australian Open on Thursday.
Lehman carded a four-under-par 68 at the Kooyonga Golf Club course, one behind Australians Shane Tait, Gary Simpson and Grant Dodd.
The American was joined on 68 by four more Australians -- Craig Parry, Brett Ogle, Neil Kerry and Matthew Goggin.

"I'm disappointed. I played one of those rounds where I could have made 62 if I'd just putted decently. Not even great, just decently," said Lehman. "To shoot 68 was by far the worst I could have shot."
Starting from the 10th, Lehman finished his first nine holes in 32 and quickly moved to four under before he dropped a shot by three-putting from 15 feet at the par four eighth.
Another former British Open champion, Ian Baker-Finch, carded a 71 to give himself a good chance of making his first halfway cut for more than a year.
The Australian, who returned last month after six months away from the game, has made the cut in only one tournament in more than two years.
